text:
### Observed differences

- The successors of A15 flipped almost completely. In the earlier window, about 82 in 100 of A15's outgoing transitions led to one of A19, A20 or A21 (about 29, 29 and 24 in 100 respectively), while A16, A17 and A18 together received only about 19 in 100. In the later window this reversed: about 79 in 100 led to A16, A17 or A18 (about 29, 22 and 29 in 100), and A19, A20 and A21 together fell to about 21 in 100. [DIR001]

- A15 moved from running together with the trio A19/A20/A21 to running together with the trio A16/A17/A18. Earlier, A15 co-occurred with each of A19, A20 and A21 in about 82 in 100 cases (always with A15 first) and with each of A16, A17 and A18 in about 19 in 100; later, these shares were about 21 in 100 for the former trio and about 79 in 100 for the latter, again always with A15 first. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]

- The two trios are mutually exclusive in both windows — no trace contains an activity from one trio together with an activity from the other. Earlier, about 82 in 100 traces carried the A19/A20/A21 trio and about 19 in 100 the A16/A17/A18 trio; later, about 79 in 100 carried the A16/A17/A18 trio and about 21 in 100 the A19/A20/A21 trio. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL018, REL019, REL020]

- Inside each trio the behaviour is unchanged: the three activities still run together and in no fixed order. Earlier, A19 preceded A20 in about 48 in 100 traces and A20 preceded A19 in about 34 in 100; later, A16 preceded A17 in about 42 in 100 and A17 preceded A16 in about 38 in 100. [REL007, REL008, REL013, REL022, REL023, REL025]

- A25 stays attached to whichever trio is active, mostly after it: with A19 it co-occurred in about 82 in 100 cases earlier (A19 first in about 46, interleaved or repeated in about 36) versus about 21 later; with A16, about 19 earlier versus about 79 later (A16 first in about 45, interleaved or repeated in about 34). [REL012, REL017, REL021, REL024, REL026, REL027]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the branch executed after A15 changed: in the earlier window, about 82 in 100 cases ran A15, then the jointly executed trio A19–A20–A21, then A25, while the alternative branch through A16–A17–A18 was taken in about 19 in 100 cases; in the later window, the A16–A17–A18 branch was taken in about 79 in 100 cases and the A19–A20–A21 branch in only about 21 in 100. This qualifies as a change in how often existing paths are taken rather than a replacement of one path by another: every activity involved is observed in both windows (each trio appears on at least about 37 of 200 traces even in its minority window), the trios remain mutually exclusive, their internal mixed order is unchanged, and A15 still precedes and A25 still follows the active trio. The flagged volume also far exceeds what a stable process produces: 28 control-flow items qualified where about 0.41 would be expected by chance across the 82 tested units, and all items describe one coherent difference — the swap in dominance between the two branches — so they are consistent rather than independent confirmations. [DIR001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a shift in the mix of cases reaching the choice point after A15 between the two windows, which would produce the same co-occurrence pattern as a modified routing decision; the exact 80/20 splits also carry sampling uncertainty inherent in finite windows. [REL009, REL022]
